question: Who has a Federal Reserve account, and who is still waiting?
answer: No crypto firm is confirmed to hold a full Federal Reserve master account. Kraken has a limited-purpose account; Anchorage Digital is waiting for a decision; Custodia Bank is fighting its denial in court.

events.what: Kansas City Fed announces it approved a limited-purpose account for Kraken Financial, classified Tier 3, for an initial term of one year, with restrictions tailored to its business.
Rep. Maxine Waters asks the Kansas City Fed to explain the legal basis, services, limits and controls of the account.

Kansas City Fed publishes the account's restrictions: Fedwire Funds only, no intraday or discount-window credit, no interest, closing-balance limit, no access for other Payward companies; says it could be viewed as a pilot of the Payment Account concept.
Sen. Blunt Rochester asks the Board and Kansas City Fed for records on the approval.
ICBA asks the Kansas City Fed to review the account and consider limits, suspension, non-renewal or termination.

items.title: Kraken (Kraken Financial)
items.sub: crypto exchange group with a state-chartered crypto bank (Wyoming SPDI)
kv: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

Only the Fedwire Funds Service (large-value wire transfers), and only in a way that rejects any payment that would overdraw the account. No intraday credit, no discount-window loans, no interest on balances, and a cap on the end-of-day balance (amount not published). Only Kraken Financial may use it; the Kraken exchange and other Payward companies may not. Initial term of one year. Kraken told Reuters it also has no FedNow or ACH access. As of mid-July 2026 Kraken's CEO said the account was not yet operating; no later public evidence of use was found.
items.text: The Kansas City Fed calls this a 'limited purpose account', not a master account; it says the decision did not create a new account category or widen who is legally eligible.
open: When does the one-year term start and end? Official sources say only 'initial term of one year'. Library dates: database Jan 28, 2026 (would end ~Jan 28, 2027) vs announcement Mar 4, 2026 (library's fed_timeline assumes Mar 4, 2027). Unresolved.
Has the account carried a first payment since the July 2026 testimony? No public evidence found through 2026-10-19.

events.what: Custodia applies to the Kansas City Fed for a master account.
Custodia sues the Board and Kansas City Fed over the delay.
The Board denies Custodia's application to become a member of the Federal Reserve System.
Kansas City Fed denies the master account request, applying the 2022 account guidelines.
District court rules for the Fed.
Tenth Circuit affirms: Reserve Banks may deny eligible institutions; eligibility is not entitlement.
Justice Gorsuch extends the petition deadline to July 11, 2026.
Custodia files its petition for certiorari (docketed July 14 as No. 26-62).
Amicus briefs filed Aug 12–13 (Blockchain Association; The Digital Chamber; Sen. Lummis and others).
The Board and the Kansas City Fed file briefs opposing Supreme Court review (after two deadline extensions).

catalog_context.title: The Fed is many legal bodies, and its building cost doubled
catalog_context.answer: The Federal Reserve remains a congressionally created system of Board, FOMC and separately chartered Reserve Banks—not a literal fourth branch—but 2026 doctrine preserves exceptional cause protection for Governors.

catalog_context.title: The OCC opened a federal trust-bank lane for crypto, but most applicants are still outside the door
catalog_context.answer: Five plainly crypto-facing national trust banks were active on the OCC's August 31 list. Circle's bank opened July 24, but it is a nondeposit custody bank—not the USDC issuer, a lender or proof of Federal Reserve access.
